cards.title: Aero Hand Open: Sim-Ready Tendon-Driven Robotic Hand with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
cards.why_it_matters: Addresses one of the hardest sim-to-real gaps in dexterous manipulation—tendon/cable transmission modeling—by releasing a complete, fully identified simulation stack that enables policy training with no real-world fine-tuning.
cards.summary: Aero Hand Open is an open-source anthropomorphic tendon-driven hand released with: a simulator that models the cable transmission directly, an identified actuation map (including three-way thumb coupling) linking motor commands to joint states bidirectionally, and an RL training package. Policies trained entirely in simulation deploy on hardware without fine-tuning or state estimation. Mechanical design, sim model, mapping, training env, and deployment stack are all released.

cards.title: Size-Weight Frontier: Principled Coverage Guarantees for Synthetic-Augmented Statistical Inference
cards.why_it_matters: Provides a theoretically grounded framework for safely weighting LLM-generated synthetic data in inference tasks—directly relevant to anyone using LLM outputs to augment limited real datasets.
cards.summary: Naively treating synthetic samples as real data biases inference. This framework characterizes augmentation by synthetic sample size and per-sample weight, then defines a size-weight frontier: for each weight, the largest synthetic sample size ensuring task-marginal coverage. The frontier is estimated from historical tasks and provides finite-sample coverage guarantees for all configurations on or below it. Applied to LLM-augmented opinion surveys, it achieves target coverage while substantially narrowing confidence intervals.

cards.title: QGPINNs: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Fractional PDEs on Quantum Graphs
cards.why_it_matters: Extends PINNs to a structurally novel domain—quantum graphs with nonlocal/fractional operators—introducing techniques like learnable singularity capture and dynamic loss balancing that could inform broader PINN architecture design.
cards.summary: QGPINNs is a PyTorch framework where each graph edge gets its own neural network; a unified loss enforces fractional elliptic and time-fractional evolution equations plus continuity, Kirchhoff-Neumann, and Dirichlet conditions. Extras include Fourier feature embeddings, soft/hard constraints, dynamic loss balancing, and a learnable singularity-capturing feature. Also supports inverse problems (recovering fractional operator orders from noisy data). Validated on IEEE 14-bus and agricultural drainage networks.

cards.title: Infinitesimal Long-Range Hoppings Nonperturbatively Reconstruct Non-Hermitian Spectra
cards.why_it_matters: Reveals a sharp, non-perturbative failure mode of standard tight-binding truncations in non-Hermitian systems—a physically important finding for anyone modeling open quantum systems or non-Hermitian skin effects.
cards.summary: Infinitesimal exponentially decaying long-range hoppings that are routinely truncated in tight-binding models can nonperturbatively reconstruct the full spectrum and eigenstates of short-range non-Hermitian systems under open boundary conditions. The effect is governed by competition between the hopping decay length and the skin-mode localization length. In 1D, a squeezed generalized Brillouin zone captures the reconstructed spectrum; in 2D+, a squeezed amoeba formulation applies. Long-range hoppings also qualitatively reshape Green's functions.

cards.title: New QFT Circuits via Mackey and Clifford Theory Yield Exponential Speedups for Non-Abelian Groups
cards.why_it_matters: Efficient QFTs over non-abelian groups are a longstanding bottleneck in quantum algorithms; these new systematic constructions unlock polynomial-in-log-q circuits for GL₂(Fq) and remove prior size restrictions for wreath products.
cards.summary: Two new approaches to non-abelian quantum Fourier transform circuit construction are introduced. The Mackey-theoretic approach yields QFT circuits over GL₂(Fq) scaling polynomially in log q rather than polynomially in q—an exponential improvement. The Clifford-theoretic approach handles wreath products F≀Sₙ with cost depending on a QFT over F and its representation registers, removing the previous |F|=poly(n) restriction and enabling exponential gains when F itself has an efficient QFT.
